items.title: 66086_Zilner T. Randolph oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] This is the one with Budd Johnson and Teddy Wilson and Yank Porter, the '33 band. [INTERVIEWEE] '33 band, yeah. Oh, uh-huh.

ctx.x: Now, the '33 band, there seemed to be more solos for the side men than in the earlier band. A lot of Budd Johnson and Keg Johnson solos.
Yes, that's right. Budd Johnson was a good tenor man, and Keg was a good -- those two Johnson boys, like, Budd (unintelligible), I mean, Keg is dead now.
Yes. Yes, he is. A fine (Unintelligible)

items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: He made an arrangement on 'Body and Soul' that we haven't played yet... he knew what he was doing.

ctx.x: (Inaudible) before we go any further, I want to ask you -- you were talking, I want you to tell me a little about Zilner Randolph about his arrangements, which (inaudible). You were saying he tried to -- what did you say about him?
Oh, man, he used to -- he used to get a kick out of seeing if he could stick us.
